messages:
ryan_sales: Quick heads-up — prospect needs SIG/CAIQ answers for encryption & key management. Questions: BYOK support, HSM compatibility/attestation, rotation cadence, and in-transit TLS for Private deployment POC. Need draft answers by EOD PST.

security_reviewer: Short answer we can reuse: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and Redwood-managed keys. For hosted: envelope encryption + integration with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. For Private: can integrate with on-prem HSM or customer KMS over VPC. Will paste a SIG-friendly paragraph below.

chris_eng: Here’s a compact paragraph for SIG / vendor risk review (feel free to trim):

```
Encryption at rest: Data stored by Redwood Inference is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Customer data encryption keys (CEKs) are envelope-encrypted with a customer-managed master key (CMK) when BYOK is enabled. Key wrapping/unwrapping operations are performed using the integrated KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or customer-supplied HSM.

In-transit: All network traffic between clients and Redwood endpoints, and between internal service components, is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites. Private deployments use customer-controlled networking (VPC) and TLS termination can be managed by the customer.

Key rotation: CEKs are rotated automatically per configured cadence (recommended 90 days). CMK rotation is controlled by the customer KMS policies; Redwood never forces CMK rotation.

Access & audit: KMS access is logged in customer or Redwood audit logs (as configured). We support HSM attestation info and can provide cryptographic module certs on request.
```

mia_prod: Add this: we never persist plaintext CEKs to disk, only in-memory cache for active sessions. Recommend adding a note about retention/zeroization on crash.

alex_sre: For the POC we can run a test BYOK flow: customer provides a CMK ARN or public-wrapped key, we validate wrap/unwrap against a staging HSM. We can produce a short checklist for network rules (VPC endpoints, firewall rules) to allow KMS traffic.

devin_ae: Prospect asked specifically for HSM attestation and FIPS level. We should state supported attestations (CloudHSM FIPS 140-2/3 on AWS; Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys; GCP Cloud KMS HSM-backed keys). Can we attach cert references?

security_reviewer: Yes — we can reference vendor certs. Uploading internal playbook link: https://redwood.internal/security/kms-playbook (internal). Also: for CAIQ map, use control ENCRYPTION-1 -> above paragraph, ENCRYPTION-2 -> key rotation details.

chris_eng: :thumbsup: I’ll DM the sample KMS policy and a trimmed paragraph for SIG.

sre_bot: deploy-checker: BYOK flow validated on staging cluster id: stg-kms-03 — run completed 2026-05-12T14:22:00Z. Tests: wrap/unwrap OK, attestation fetched.

ryan_sales: Awesome — I’ll paste the draft into the SIG questionnaire and send it off. Can someone DM me the sample KMS policy + the POC steps (network checklist + minimal commands)? :pray:

alex_sre: Will DM the checklist in 10.

mia_prod: Sending the zeroization notes and rotation recommendation now.

devin_ae: I’ll attach vendor cert links to the CAIQ response before submission.

security_reviewer: If they ask for an SLA clause about key handling in Private, we have a template (internal). Link in the playbook.

ryan_sales: Thanks team, really helps. Will update thread after I hear back from the customer's security contact.
